What this group needs to understand

01

Common, treatable, never a personal failing

10.5% of 11-17 year olds meet the criteria for major depressive disorder. Young Australians rank it the 2nd most urgent national issue.

02

Help-seeking is a skill, not a weakness

Three of four affected adolescents never access professional help. We teach who to approach, what to say, what happens next.

03

Every student is a first responder

Young people disclose to friends, not adults. Bully-victims carry 4.3× the risk of suicidal ideation. Bystanders matter.

Lived-experience stories reduce stigma and raise help-seeking intentions.
(Lawrence et al., 2015 · Berger et al., 2020 · Ford et al., 2017)
Friends notice first

Whole-school. Universal. Tiered.

0

records screened by the rapid review for the NSW Department of Education

The most effective programs were universal and whole-school, with age-specific content in sequence. Stand-alone programs such as the Resourceful Adolescent Program produced no significant reduction.

Y5-6Name itEmotional literacy. No suicide content.

Y10-12Respond safelyPrevention inside general mental health.
Y5Y12

One continuous sequence, every year, no gaps.

No Australian program runs continuously from Year 5 to Year 12. Ours would.
Ottawa Charter: Develop personal skills · sessions Create supportive environments · staff training Strengthen community action · student campaign
(Berger et al., 2020)

Three stages, one line.

Years 5 to 12 on one continuous line. Each stage rehearses a skill. No stand-alone suicide lessons.

Y5–6

Name it

Emotional literacy, spotting persistent low mood, asking for help. No suicide content.

Y7–9

Understand it

Symptoms, causes, treatability, coping, spotting distress in peers.

Y10–12

Respond safely

Prevention inside general mental health promotion, following headspace advice.

(headspace, n.d. · Wasserman et al., 2015 · McGillivray et al., 2021)

What makes it stick

01 · Strengths first

Every tier opens with a strengths assessment. One-off workshops measure satisfaction; ours measures skills, in-curriculum.

02 · Teen MHFA

Years 7-12 complete three 75-minute peer-support sessions. An Australian trial found lasting first-aid confidence at 12 months.

03 · Student-led campaign

Student leaders run the awareness campaign every August, anchored to Bullying No Way Week.

04 · The plan card

Every student keeps warning signs, two strategies, one trusted adult — revisited yearly.

Sleep is the named pillar: close to 60% of 16-17 year olds with anxiety or depression symptoms miss the minimum guidelines.

6 in 10 miss guidelines16-17 y/o
(MyStrengths, n.d. · Hart et al., 2022 · Mental Health First Aid Australia, n.d.)

Realistic. Feasible. Measured.

Measure yearly. Do not judge until year 6 — whole-school programs need time.

Curriculum timeInside existing PDHPE lessons — no extra timetable.
